title: Telugu

how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Telugu voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Telugu in Roman letters, and let the script come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn the Telugu script before speaking?

hfaqs.a: నమస్కారం for respect, అవును and కాదు, ధన్యవాదాలు, దయచేసి, సరే, and నేను — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Telugu states politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The retroflex family new to most ears — ళ, ణ, the trilled ఱ, long-short vowel pairs. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Telugu?

topics.desc: నమస్కారం opens every door in Telugu states — plus mornings, welcomes and warm goodbyes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes, and nobody will mind — నమస్కారం with folded hands is understood and loved everywhere Telugu is spoken. With close friends a smile and బాగున్నారా? (are you well?) feels warmer.
faqs.q: Can I just say namaskaram everywhere?

faqs.a: నమస్కారం with folded hands and a small nod, and మీరు (meeru — formal you) until invited closer. Add అన్నయ్య (annayya) or అక్కయ్య (akkayya) for someone slightly older — it warms everything instantly.
faqs.q: How do I greet an elder respectfully?

faqs.a: మళ్లీ కలుద్దాం (mallee kaluddaam — we'll meet again) is the warm standard. సెలవు (selavu — permission to leave) is the classic respectful farewell — receive it with a smile and a nod.
faqs.q: How do Telugu people say goodbye?

topics.note: A note on బాగున్నారా vs కులాసా. బాగున్నారా? (baagunnaaraa) is the everyday are you well? — warm, quick, everywhere. కులాసాగా ఉన్నారా? is its old-fashioned formal cousin, heard from grandparents. Start with బాగున్నారా; the rest arrives with aunties.
paras: నమస్కారం (namaskaram) is the one greeting that never fails. Folded hands, a small nod, and it works with strangers, elders, shopkeepers and officials — exactly the people a learner meets first. Say it clearly, hold the folded hands half a second, and the Telugu states open to you.

Mornings get their own greeting: శుభోదయం (shubhodayam — good morning), heard in offices, schools and tiffin centres until about eleven. Evenings soften to శుభసాయంత్రం (shubhasaayantram). Time-stamped greetings signal that you live in the language, not just visit it.

Welcomes are grand in Telugu culture: స్వాగతం (svaagatam — welcome) opens homes, shops and hearts. Guests are greeted standing, often with water or coffee before a single question. Return the warmth — వచ్చాను, ధన్యవాదాలు (I've come, thank you) — and you are family within minutes.

Goodbyes promise return, never end: మళ్లీ కలుద్దాం (we'll meet again) is the everyday farewell; జాగ్రత్త (jaagratta — take care) adds affection. Leave every conversation with a నమస్కారం and a smile — in Telugu culture, how you leave is remembered longer than how you came.
topics.title: Saying hello the Telugu way

topics.desc: Vowels, consonants, gunintalu and the trilled ఱ — the Telugu alphabet without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sixteen vowels (అచ్చులు) and thirty-seven consonants (హల్లులు) — 53+ letters that combine into gunintalu. Sounds huge, behaves simply: learn the shapes and the combinations assemble themselves.
faqs.q: How many letters does Telugu have?

faqs.a: ఱ (rra) — the alveolar trill, rolled hard, found in old pure-Telugu words. Modern speech often merges it with ర, but reading classics demands it. Listen, roll, practise.
faqs.q: What is the hardest Telugu letter?

faqs.a: Yes — in writing: ఖ ఘ ఛ ఝ ఠ ఢ థ ధ ఫ భ appear in Sanskrit loans (క్షమ, ధర్మం). Daily Telugu softens most of them; recognise them in print, relax in speech.
faqs.q: Does Telugu have kh, gh, bh sounds?

topics.note: A note on the sunna (ం). The little circle above a syllable nasalises it: క is ka, కం is kam. Telugu writes pure nasals with the sunna and full conjuncts without — అం + క = అంక. One circle, and the whole nasal system clicks.
paras: Telugu vowels (అచ్చులు) come in sixteen: అ ఆ ఇ ఈ ఉ ఊ ఋ ౠ ఎ ఏ ఐ ఒ ఓ ఔ అం అః. Short and long pairs — అ/ఆ, ఇ/ఈ, ఉ/ఊ — change meaning completely: కల (kala — dream) versus కాలం (kaalam — time). Length is meaning in Telugu; stretch with care.

Consonants (హల్లులు) run five rows deep: క ఖ గ ఘ ఙ, చ ఛ జ ఝ ఞ, ట ఠ డ ఢ ణ, త థ ద ధ న, ప ఫ బ భ మ — plus య ర ల వ శ ష స హ ళ క్ష ఱ. Call it the Italian of the East: nearly every word ends in a vowel, and the script rounds every corner.

Vowels and consonants marry into గుణింతాలు (gunintalu): క్ + అ = క (ka), క్ + ఆ = కా (kaa). Learn the twelve vowel-signs once and every consonant sings the same song — the system is vast but perfectly regular.

Then the crown jewels: ఱ (rra), the trilled warrior of old Telugu — ఱెక్క, కఱకు; and ళ (lla), the retroflex liquid — పళ్ళు, వేళ. Natives will grin when you land them; the grin is worth weeks of practice.
topics.title: Telugu alphabet

topics.desc: ఒకటి రెండు మూడు to వంద — plus clock time and market-ready counting. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: International digits for daily life — prices, phones, buses all use them. Telugu has traditional number words in full use (ఒకటి, పది, వంద) but modern digits in print.
faqs.q: Telugu digits or international digits?

faqs.a: Take the number, add గంటలు (gantalu — hours): మూడు గంటలు (three o'clock). Half past addsన్నర — మూడున్నర is half past three. One rule, every clock in Telugu states.
faqs.q: How do I say the time in Telugu?

faqs.a: ఎంత? (enta — how much?). Then listen for the number plus రూపాయలు (roopaayalu — rupees). Market Telugu is the fastest teacher there is.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

topics.lede: ఒకటి రెండు మూడు — numbers, clock time and market-ready counting.

links.desc: Numbers in course order, with drills.
links.label: Telugu numbers

topics.note: A note on ఒంటిగంట, రెండుగంటలు. One o'clock is ఒంటిగంట (ontiganta — special form!), two onwards take గంటలు — రెండు గంటలు, ఐదు గంటలు. Every language hides one irregular clock word; Telugu's is ఒంటిగంట. Learn it and sound native instantly.
paras: One to ten: ఒకటి (okati), రెండు (rendu), మూడు (moodu), నాలుగు (naalugu), ఐదు (aidu), ఆరు (aaru), ఏడు (edu), ఎనిమిది (enimidi), తొమ్మిది (tommidi), పది (padi). Chant them in rhythm — Telugu numbers love rhythm — and they stick in days, not weeks.

Eleven to nineteen build on పది: పదకొండు (11), పన్నెండు (12), పదమూడు (13)... then the tens march: ఇరవై (20), ముప్పై (30), నలభై (40), యాభై (50), అరవై (60), డెబ్బై (70), ఎనభై (80), తొంభై (90), వంద (100). Past twenty, glue tens to units — ఇరవై ఒకటి (21) — and count to a thousand (వెయ్యి) without fear.

Money runs on numbers: the currency is the రూపాయి (roopaayi — rupee), and ఎంత? (enta — how much?) is the most useful sentence in Telugu states. Listen for the number, repeat it back — యాభై? (fifty?) — and your first Telugu transaction completes itself.

Time reuses numbers with గంట (ganta — hour): రెండు గంటలు (two o'clock), ఐదు గంటలు (five o'clock). ఇప్పుడు టైమ్ ఎంత? (what time is it now?) is the question; half hours add -న్నర. Numbers, money, clocks: one skill, three daily victories.
topics.title: Counting in Telugu

topics.desc: Names, homes and small talk — your first real Telugu conversations, line by line. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: మీ పేరు ఏమిటి? (mee peru emiti — what is your name?) for respect; నీ పేరు ఏమిటి? (nee peru emiti) for friends and children. Answer with నా పేరు... (naa peru — my name is...). Names first, always.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: మీరు ఎక్కడి నుండి వస్తున్నారు? (where are you from?) — then answer for yourself: నేను ... నుండి వస్తున్నాను. Origin questions are the universal second question; prepare your answer before you need it.
faqs.q: How do I say where I'm from?

faqs.a: నెమ్మదిగా మాట్లాడండి (please speak slowly) and మళ్లీ చెప్పండి (please say it again). Said with a smile, these two sentences make every Telugu speaker slow down and help.
faqs.q: What do I say when people speak too fast?

topics.note: A note on మీరు, నువ్వు and గారు. Telugu has two yous where English has one: మీరు (meeru — formal/plural) and నువ్వు (nuvvu — familiar) — plus the magic suffix గారు (gaaru) that elevates any name. Start with మీరు for every adult; let friendship invite you to నువ్వు.
paras: Every first conversation follows the same dance: నమస్కారం, మీ పేరు ఏమిటి? (what is your name?), నా పేరు... (my name is...), మీరు ఎక్కడి నుండి వస్తున్నారు? (where are you from?). Four lines, and you have had a real conversation. Practise them in order until they flow without thinking.

Small talk runs on three questions: మీరు ఏమి చేస్తారు? (what do you do?), తెలుగు మాట్లాడతారా? (do you speak Telugu?), భోజనం చేశారా? (have you eaten? — asked with genuine care). Answer briefly, ask back immediately — మీరు? — because conversations are volleys, not speeches.

When the torrent comes — and Telugu hospitality pours words — deploy the brakes: నెమ్మదిగా మాట్లాడండి (please speak slowly), నాకు అర్థం కాలేదు (I didn't understand), మళ్లీ చెప్పండి (please say it again). Every Telugu speaker honours these instantly; they are the learner's seatbelt.

Close warmly and promise return: మిమ్మల్ని కలవడం సంతోషం (pleased to meet you), మళ్లీ కలుద్దాం (we'll meet again). Leave with a నమస్కారం and the door stays open — Telugu conversations end the way they begin: with folded hands.
topics.title: Real Telugu conversation

topics.desc: వెళ్ళు, రా, తిను — the twelve verbs that run daily life, plus how they bend. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Stems are orders to friends — వెళ్ళు! (go!), రా! (come!), తిను! (eat!). Polite speech adds endings: వెళ్లండి (please go), రండి (please come). Learn stems first, politeness second, and never order a stranger.
faqs.q: Are verb stems commands?

faqs.a: నేను వెళ్తున్నాను (I go), నువ్వు వెళ్తున్నావు (you go), అతను వెళ్తున్నాడు (he goes). Person-markers on every verb — drill one verb through all persons and the pattern owns you.
faqs.q: How do Telugu verbs change?

faqs.a: లేదు (ledu — no/not) negates existence — నాకు తెలియదు uses -దు for verbs (I don't know). Telugu negation splits by word type; learn లేదు for things, వద్దు (vaddu — don't want) for refusals.
faqs.q: How do I say no to a verb?

topics.note: A note on రండి vs రా. రా (raa) orders a friend to come; రండి (randi) welcomes a guest like royalty. Same verb, different universe — the -అండి ending is pure respect. When in doubt, add the respect: Telugu people forgive stiff politeness instantly and casual rudeness never.
paras: Twelve verbs carry daily life: వెళ్ళు (go), రా (come), తిను (eat), త్రాగు (drink), చదువు (read/study), రాయి (write), చేయి (do), మాట్లాడు (speak), ఇవ్వు (give), తీసుకో (take), ఉండు (be/stay), చూడు (see). Memorise these stems and you can order food, find toilets, make friends and survive beautifully.

Stems bend by person in the present: నేను వెళ్తున్నాను (I go), నువ్వు వెళ్తున్నావు (you familiar go), మీరు వెళ్తున్నారు (you formal go), అతను వెళ్తున్నాడు (he goes). The -తున్న- (tunna) infix marks present tense across nearly every verb — one infix, hundreds of verbs, instant sentences.

Polite commands add -అండి: వెళ్లండి (please go), రండి (please come), తినండి (please eat), చెప్పండి (please say). This one ending turns every order into an invitation — it is the most useful suffix in Telugu, worth more than a hundred nouns.

Negation and existence close the kit: ఉంది (undi — it is / there is) anchors locations — పుస్తకం టేబుల్ మీద ఉంది (the book is on the table). లేదు (ledu — there isn't) removes — డబ్బు లేదు (no money). Twelve verbs plus ఉంది/లేదు: the engine room of Telugu.

topics.desc: Water, money, time, today — the everyday Telugu words that unlock daily life. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Time words first: ఈరోజు (today), రేపు (tomorrow), నిన్న (yesterday), ఇప్పుడు (now). You will use them ten times a day — shopping, planning, chatting — while rare nouns gather dust.
faqs.q: Which words pay off fastest?

faqs.a: Telugu happily absorbs English — బస్సు (bus), టికెట్ (ticket), ఆఫీసు (office). Use the pure Telugu word when you know it, the loanword when you don't. Fluency first, purity later.
faqs.q: Is mixing English okay?

faqs.a: Nouns first, verbs second, adjectives third. With fifty nouns and the twelve verbs from the verbs page, you can point, ask and survive — grammar glues them later.
faqs.q: Nouns or verbs first?

topics.note: A note on ఈరోజు, రేపు, నిన్న. Telugu time words pivot around today: ఈరోజు (eeroju — today), రేపు (repu — tomorrow), నిన్న (ninna — yesterday). Master this trio and half your daily sentences assemble themselves — రేపు కలుద్దాం (see you tomorrow) alone is worth the lesson.
paras: Survival runs on nouns: నీళ్లు (neellu — water), ఆహారం (aahaaram — food), ఇల్లు (illu — home), డబ్బు (dabbu — money), సమయం (samayam — time). Five words, and you can ask for water, find home, handle money and ask the time — the entire first day in a new city.

Movement words come next: రోడ్డు (roaddu — road), బస్సు (bassu — bus), దుకాణం (dukaanam — shop), బడి (badi — school). Telugu cities move by bus and foot; knowing బస్ స్టాండ్ ఎక్కడ? (where is the bus stand?) saves more time than any app.

Opinions need adjectives: మంచి (manchi — good), పెద్ద (pedda — big), చిన్న (chinna — small), కొత్త (kotta — new), పాత (paata — old). మంచిది (manchidi — that's good) approves everything from food to plans — the most useful single opinion in Telugu.

Weather and mood close the kit: వాన (vaana — rain) matters half the year, ఎండ (enda — sun/heat) the other half. వాన పడుతోంది (rain is coming) starts conversations with strangers; in Telugu states, weather talk is friendship's front door.

topics.desc: Idli, dosa, biryani — order like a local, from breakfast to bill. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Point and say ఇది ఒకటి (idi okati — one of these) — it works in every mess, canteen and bakery in Telugu states. Add దయచేసి (please) and a smile; grammar can wait until dessert.
faqs.q: How do I order with almost no Telugu?

faqs.a: కారం తక్కువ (kaaram takkuva — less spicy, please). Telugu food honours chilli deeply — Gongura, avakaya; this one sentence saves sensitive stomachs while keeping every flavour.
faqs.q: How do I ask for less spicy food?

faqs.a: రుచిగా ఉంది (ruchigaa undi — it's delicious). Say it to the cook, the server, the auntie who packed your lunch — it is the highest compliment in Telugu food culture.
faqs.q: How do I praise the food?

topics.note: A note on బిర్యానీ. Hyderabadi biryani — dum-cooked, saffron-scented, argued over passionately — is not dinner, it is identity. Order చికెన్ బిర్యానీ at any old-city hotel, eat with mirchi ka salan and raita, and understand Hyderabad in one plate.
paras: Breakfast is the glory: ఇడ్లీ (idlee — steamed rice cakes), దోస (dosa — crisp crepe), పూరీ (pooree — puffed bread), వడ (vada — savoury doughnut), all served with సాంబారు (saambaaru) and చట్నీ (chutney). టిఫిన్ చేశారా? (have you had tiffin?) is asked with love — answer honestly, then accept seconds.

Meals centre on భోజనం (bhojanam — the rice meal): rice, పప్పు (pappu — dal), సాంబారు, రసం (rasam — pepper-tamarind soup), పెరుగు (perugu — curd), అప్పడం (appadam — crisp papad). Served on banana leaves at weddings, eaten with the right hand — భోజనం రెడీనా? (is the meal ready?) is the happiest question.

Taste words steer every order: కారం (kaaram — spicy), తీపి (teepi — sweet), పులుపు (pulupu — sour), ఉప్పు (uppu — salt). కొంచెం ఉప్పు (a little salt), చక్కెర వద్దు (no sugar) — with taste words, your plate obeys you.

Drinks and bills close the meal: కాఫీ (coffee), టీ (tea), మజ్జిగ (majjiga — buttermilk), పండ్లరసం (pandlarasam — juice). బిల్లు ఇవ్వండి (please give the bill) ends it; రుచిగా ఉంది (it was delicious) guarantees a smile on your way out.
topics.title: Food phrases

topics.desc: ర vs ఱ, ళ, క్ష — every tricky Telugu sound, one by one, with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Mostly — modern speech merges them in daily words, but classics, names and careful speech keep ఱ trilled. Learn to hear it first; roll it second. Reading old poetry demands it.
faqs.q: Do ర and ఱ really differ?

faqs.a: ళ is retroflex — tongue curled back: పళ్ళు (teeth), వేళ (finger/time). ల is dental — tongue on teeth: పలు? Say la-la sliding tongue back and feel the shift.
faqs.q: How do I make the ళ sound?

faqs.a: Conjuncts: క్ష (ksha — క్షమ), జ్ఞ (jna — జ్ఞానం), త్ర (tra). Pronounce each part quickly in sequence — k+sha, j+na. Conjuncts look fierce and behave kindly.
faqs.q: What are those stacked letters?

topics.note: A note on ఱ (rra). Telugu's warrior trill: roll it hard like Spanish rr — ఱెక్క (wing), కఱకు (rough). Daily speech often softens it toward ర, but names, proverbs and poetry keep the trill. Roll boldly; natives applaud the effort.
paras: The two r's split soft and hard: ర is a light flap — నోరు (noru — mouth), మరి (mari — well then) — while ఱ trills hard — ఱెక్క (rrekka — wing). English ears merge them; Telugu meaning doesn't. Practise pairs daily until your tongue files them separately.

The liquid ళ curls back: పళ్ళు (pallu — teeth), వేళ (vela — time/finger), పల్లె (palle — village) Keep it clean: contrast ల (dental, tongue on teeth) with ళ (retroflex, curled). Glide la-lla daily; the roof-touch becomes reflex.

Dental versus retroflex stops: త (teeth — తలుపు, తెలుగు) against ట (roof — కోట, అట్ట?). Hold a finger to your lips: dentals puff forward, retroflexes pop upward. Ten minutes of త-ట alternation retunes the mouth within a week.

Conjuncts stack kindly: క్ష (ksha — క్షమ, forgiveness), జ్ఞ (jna — జ్ఞానం, knowledge), చ (cha — చెట్టు, tree; softening to sa inside words). Telugu spelling mirrors speech faithfully: pronounce what you see, and you are right nine times in ten.
topics.title: Telugu pronunciation

topics.desc: Verb last, respect built in — Telugu grammar in plain English, no jargon walls. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Put the verb last: నేను పుస్తకం చదువుతున్నాను (I book read). Subject-Object-Verb, always. English instincts will fight you for a week; then SOV feels like home.
faqs.q: Where does the verb go?

faqs.a: నాకు (naaku — to me), నీకు (neeku — to you familiar), మీకు (meeku — to you formal). నాకు నీళ్లు కావాలి (I want water) is literally to-me water is-wanted — Telugu wants flow toward people.
faqs.q: How do I say I want something?

faqs.a: ఇది (idi — this, near me), అది (adi — that, far). ఇది ఏమిటి? (what is this?) points at anything within reach; mastery takes one shopping trip.
faqs.q: How do this and that work?

topics.note: A note on -కు (ku). Telugu's dative ending aims verbs at people and places: నాకు (to me), బడికి (to school), ఇంటికి (homeward). Sentences like నాకు అర్థమైంది (to-me it-is-understood = I understand) reveal Telugu's worldview: experiences come TO you.
paras: Telugu sentences end with the verb: నేను పుస్తకం చదువుతున్నాను (I — book — read). Subject first, object middle, verb last — SOV, the order of half the world's languages. Rearrange your English instincts once, and every Telugu sentence parses cleanly.

Small endings do heavy work: -లో (lo — in/on) places things — ఇంట్లో (at home), టేబులు మీద (on the table); -తో (to — with) joins company — స్నేహితుడితో (with a friend); -కు (ku) aims motion and wanting — బడికి (to school), నాకు కావాలి (I want). Endings, not word order, carry Telugu meaning.

Questions rise at the end: మీరు ఎక్కడికి వెళ్తున్నారు? (where are you going?) — ఎక్కడ (where), ఏమిటి (what), ఎవరు (who), ఎందుకు (why), ఎలా (how), ఎప్పుడు (when). Yes-no questions add -ఆ (-aa): భోజనం చేశారా? (have you eaten?). Question words plus rising tone — asking is easy.

Negation splits three ways: లేదు (ledu) denies existence — డబ్బు లేదు (no money); verb endings deny actions — నాకు తెలియదు (I don't know); వద్దు (vaddu) refuses — చక్కెర వద్దు (no sugar, thanks). Three no's for three jobs — Telugu refuses precisely.

phrases.en: I read a book (I book read)

topics.desc: Your first Telugu week: yes, no, I, you, and ten sentences that survive anything. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: నమస్కారం, అవును, సరే, ధన్యవాదాలు, దయచేసి — five words, infinite mileage. Add నేను and మీరు and you can introduce yourself to anyone in Telugu states.
faqs.q: What are the first five words?

faqs.a: Fifteen focused minutes beat two distracted hours. One topic page, every speaker tapped, five words reviewed — daily beats heroic.
faqs.q: How much should I study daily?

faqs.a: No — speak first, script second. Roman letters carry you through months of conversation; the alphabet page waits patiently until curiosity pulls you in.
faqs.q: Must I learn the script first?

topics.lede: Your first Telugu week: yes, no, I, you, and sentences that survive anything.

links.desc: The course start, step by step.
links.label: Telugu beginner course

topics.note: A note on అవును, సరే and ఊ. Telugu yes comes in three flavours: అవును (avunu — respectful yes), సరే (sare — okay/agreed), ఊ (oo — casual yeah). Learners live on అవును and సరే — respectful, warm, never wrong. Save ఊ for friends.
paras: Week one needs eleven words: నమస్కారం (hello), అవును (yes), సరే (okay), ధన్యవాదాలు (thanks), దయచేసి (please), నేను (I), మీరు (you, formal), ఇది ఏమిటి? (what is this?), అర్థమైంది (I understand), తెలియదు (I don't know), వెళ్దాం (let's go). Eleven words, and you can greet, agree, thank, ask, confess ignorance and move — the whole beginner game.

Pronouns branch early: నేను (I), మీరు (you formal/plural), నువ్వు (you familiar), అతను/ఆమె (he/she), వారు (they formal), మేము (we exclusive), మనం (we inclusive). Two we's where English has one — మనం వెళ్దాం (let's go, you included) is Telugu's warmest invitation.

Quantity words multiply everything: కొంచెం (a little), చాలా (a lot), చాలు (enough), మాత్రమే (only). కొంచెం తెలుగు మాట్లాడతాను (I speak a little Telugu) is the perfect learner's confession — humble, charming, instantly rewarded with help.

Action invitations close week one: ఇక్కడికి రండి (come here), కూర్చోండి (please sit), తినండి (please eat), వెళ్దాం (let's go). These four run hospitality, the beating heart of Telugu culture — learn them and you stop being a guest and start being family.
topics.title: Telugu for absolute beginners

topics.desc: అమ్మ, నాన్న, అన్నయ్య, అక్క — family words, including the elder-younger split. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Yes — Telugu splits siblings by age: అన్నయ్య (elder brother) versus తమ్ముడు (younger brother), అక్క (elder sister) versus చెల్లెలు (younger sister). Age order is grammar in Telugu families.
faqs.q: Why two words for brother?

faqs.a: అన్నయ్య (annayya) and అక్కయ్య (akkayya) address any slightly-older man or woman — shopkeepers, colleagues, strangers. It borrows family warmth for the whole world.
faqs.q: Can I call strangers annayya and akkayya?

faqs.a: మీ కుటుంబంలో ఎంతమంది? (how many people in your family?) — then listen proudly to the answer. Family questions are love in Telugu culture.
faqs.q: How do I ask about family?

topics.lede: అమ్మ, నాన్న, అన్నయ్య, అక్క — family, including the elder-younger split.
topics.note: A note on అమ్మమ్మ vs నానమ్మ. Telugu grandmothers split by side: అమ్మమ్మ (mother's mother) versus నానమ్మ (father's mother) — and తాతయ్య covers grandfathers with side-names too. Learners need the big six first; the full map unfolds at weddings.
paras: Parents anchor everything: అమ్మ (amma — mother) and నాన్న (naanna — father) — the first words of every Telugu child and the warmest words in the language. అమ్మ calls across market crowds; నాన్న advises over evening coffee. Learn them with love, not just memory.

Siblings split by age, never blend: అన్నయ్య (elder brother), తమ్ముడు (younger brother), అక్క (elder sister), చెల్లెలు (younger sister). There is no plain brother — every brother is elder or younger, and the word you choose declares the hierarchy. Ask ages early; address correctly always.

Grandparents rule the roost: తాతయ్య (taatayya — grandfather) and అమ్మమ్మ/నానమ్మ (grandmothers) — storytellers, sweet-sneakers, family courts of final appeal. అమ్మమ్మ కథ (grandmother's tale) is a whole genre; తాతయ్య advice ends arguments. Respect flows upward; treats flow down.

The wider net holds daily life: మామయ్య (uncle), అత్తయ్య (auntie), భర్త (husband), భార్య (wife), కుటుంబం (family itself). నా కుటుంబం (my family) introduces them all — practise the sentence with your own names filled in, because you will say it at every Telugu gathering forever.
topics.title: Family words

topics.desc: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Telugu time from morning to month. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start the week Sunday like Telugu calendars: ఆదివారం, సోమవారం, మంగళవారం, బుధవారం, గురువారం, శుక్రవారం, శనివారం. Chant them in order — rhythm makes them permanent.
faqs.q: How do I memorise the days?

faqs.a: ఉదయం (morning), మధ్యాహ్నం (afternoon), సాయంత్రం (evening), రాత్రి (night). Greetings, meals and plans all key off these four — శుభసాయంత్రం (good evening) after four-ish.
faqs.q: How does Telugu split the day?

faqs.a: వారం (vaaram — week), నెల (nela — month), సంవత్సరం (samvatsaram — year). వచ్చే వారం (next week), ఈ నెల (this month) — plans assemble instantly.
faqs.q: Week, month, year?

topics.lede: Seven days, four day-parts, weeks and months — Telugu time fully told.

links.desc: Clocks and calendars in course order.
links.label: Telugu time and dates

topics.note: A note on శుక్రవారం and మంగళవారం. Friday (శుక్రవారం) and Tuesday (మంగళవారం) are auspicious days — temples fill, new ventures launch, అమ్మవారి worship peaks. Knowing the days means knowing the rhythm: never schedule a sceptical meeting on a festival Friday.
paras: The week runs Sunday-first: ఆదివారం (Sunday), సోమవారం (Monday), మంగళవారం (Tuesday), బుధవారం (Wednesday), గురువారం (Thursday), శుక్రవారం (Friday), శనివారం (Saturday). Planet-named like most of Asia — the sky keeps Telugu's calendar, and every day ends in వారం.

Day-parts steer greetings and meals: ఉదయం (morning — శుభోదయం), మధ్యాహ్నం (afternoon — lunch/bhojanam o'clock), సాయంత్రం (evening — శుభసాయంత్రం, coffee round two), రాత్రి (night — goodnight is usually just నమస్కారం with a smile).

Bigger units plan life: వారం (week), నెల (month), సంవత్సరం (year) — వచ్చే వారం (next week), గత నెల (last month), ఈ సంవత్సరం (this year). Telugu plans in weeks for errands, months for visits, years for weddings.

Dates assemble simply: తేదీ (tedee — date), మొదటి తేదీ (first), ఈరోజు తేదీ ఎంత? (what's today's date?). Numbers from the numbers page slot straight in — పదిహేనవ తేదీ (the 15th). Time, dates, plans: one page, total coverage.
topics.title: Time and dates

topics.desc: Stations, directions, tickets and toilets — travel Telugu that gets you there. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ...ఎక్కడ? (...ekkada — where is...?) plus a pointing finger. బస్ స్టాండ్ ఎక్కడ? రైల్వే స్టేషన్ ఎక్కడ? One pattern, every destination in Telugu states.
faqs.q: How do I ask where things are?

faqs.a: ఎడమ (left), కుడి (right), నేరుగా (straight) — then దగ్గర (near) and దూరం (far). Telugu directions come with generous hand-waving; watch the hands as well as the words.
faqs.q: Left, right, straight?

faqs.a: టాయిలెట్ ఎక్కడ? (where is the toilet?) — say it clearly, without embarrassment. Every bus stand, station and restaurant understands instantly.
faqs.q: How do I find a toilet?

topics.note: A note on స్టేషన్. స్టేషన్ (station) anchors every journey: బస్ స్టాండ్ (bus stand), రైల్వే స్టేషన్ (railway station), విమానాశ్రయం (airport). Learn the pattern once — vehicle + స్టేషన్ — and every signboard in Telugu states reads itself.
paras: Destinations unlock with one pattern: బస్ స్టాండ్ (bus stand), రైల్వే స్టేషన్ (railway station), విమానాశ్రయం (airport), హోటల్ (hotel). Add ఎక్కడ? (where?) and you can find every transport hub in the states — స్టేషన్ ఎక్కడ? is the traveller's master key.

Directions come in threes: ఎడమ (left), కుడి (right), నేరుగా (straight ahead) — plus దగ్గర (nearby) and దూరం (far). ఎడమ వైపు (on the left side), నేరుగా వెళ్లండి (go straight) — follow the words, watch the inevitable hand gestures, arrive smiling.

Tickets and seats run the journey: టికెట్ (ticket), ఒక టికెట్ (one ticket), ఎంత? (how much?), సీటు (seatu — seat). బస్సు ఎప్పుడు వస్తుంది? (when does the bus come?) — asked at every stand, answered with cheerful vagueness. Patience is also vocabulary.

Emergencies and essentials close the kit: సహాయం (help), టాయిలెట్ ఎక్కడ? (where is the toilet?), నీళ్లు (water), ఆసుపత్రి (hospital). Hope never to need నాకు సహాయం చేయండి (please help) — but carry it always, like travel insurance in a single word.
topics.title: Travel phrases

topics.desc: Prices, bargaining and colours — shop in Telugu from first price to final deal. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ధర ఎంత? (what's the price?) — then ఎంత? (how much?) for everything else. Two questions, every shop in Telugu states.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

faqs.a: చాలా ఖరీదు (too costly) with a smile, then కొంచెం తగ్గించండి (reduce a little, please). Bargaining is friendly theatre — play your part warmly and the price moves.
faqs.q: How do I bargain politely?

faqs.a: Start with five: ఎరుపు (red), నీలం (blue), ఆకుపచ్చ (green), పసుపు (yellow), తెలుపు (white). వేరే రంగు (different colour) shows them all.
faqs.q: Which colours first?

topics.note: A note on తగ్గించండి. కొంచెం తగ్గించండి (konchem tagginchandi — please reduce a little) is the magic sentence of Telugu markets. Said smiling, it opens every negotiation; said with కొంటాను (I'll buy it) right after, it closes most. Bargaining respects the dance — never the demand.
paras: Prices open every transaction: ధర ఎంత? (what's the price?), ఎంత? (how much?), ఇది ధర ఎంత? (what's this one's price?). Listen for the number plus రూపాయలు — repeat it back to confirm — యాభై? (fifty?) — and you are already shopping in Telugu.

Bargaining follows the friendly script: చాలా ఖరీదు (too costly), కొంచెం తగ్గించండి (reduce a little), డిస్కౌంట్ ఉందా? (any discount?). Start walking away slowly — ధన్యవాదాలు, చూస్తాను (thanks, I'll look around) — and the real price often chases you down the street.

Sizes and colours refine the hunt: పెద్దది (the bigger one), చిన్నది (the smaller one), కొత్తది (a new one), వేరే రంగు (a different colour). Point, name the change, nod — Telugu shopkeepers read gestures fluently and reward attempts instantly.

Colours close the sale: ఎరుపు (red), నీలం (blue), ఆకుపచ్చ (green), పసుపు (yellow), తెలుపు (white), నలుపు (black). ఎరుపు బాగుంది (the red looks good) — then కొంటాను (I'll take it). Deal done, in Telugu, with a smile on both sides.
topics.title: Shopping and bargaining

topics.desc: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Telugu you hope to never need. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: నాకు సహాయం చేయండి (please help me) — loud, clear, repeated. Add ఆసుపత్రి ఎక్కడ? (where is the hospital?) and Telugu crowds mobilise instantly.
faqs.q: What is the one emergency sentence?

faqs.a: Point and say ఇక్కడ నొప్పిగా ఉంది (it hurts here). Then ఒంట్లో బాగోలేదు (I feel unwell) and డాక్టర్ కావాలి (I need a doctor). Pain plus pointing crosses every language gap.
faqs.q: How do I explain pain?

faqs.a: పోయింది (it is lost) — డబ్బు పోయింది (money lost), బ్యాగ్ పోయింది (bag lost). Then పోలీస్ స్టేషన్ ఎక్కడ? (where is the police station?).
faqs.q: How do I report something lost?

topics.lede: Help, doctor, hospital — emergency Telugu you hope to never need.
topics.note: A note on సహాయం. సహాయం (sahaayam — help) is Telugu's shortest lifeline — shout it and crowds come running. Telugu bystander culture is famously kind: strangers will escort you to hospitals, translate for doctors, and refuse thanks. Ask loudly; receive gratefully.
paras: The core three save lives: సహాయం (help), ప్రమాదం (danger), అత్యవసరం (emergency). నాకు సహాయం చేయండి (please help me) — say it to anyone, anywhere. Telugu crowds respond to distress calls faster than any app; your job is only to ask.

Medical words route the rescue: డాక్టర్ (doctor), ఆసుపత్రి (hospital), మందు (medicine), మందుల షాపు (pharmacy). ఆసుపత్రి ఎక్కడ? (where is the hospital?) plus a taxi wave — in cities, help arrives in minutes.

Symptoms speak simply: ఇక్కడ నొప్పిగా ఉంది (it hurts here — point!), ఒంట్లో బాగోలేదు (I feel unwell), తలనొప్పి (headache), జ్వరం (fever). Pain words plus pointing hands diagnose across every language barrier on earth.

Danger and loss close the kit: అగ్ని (fire), దొంగ (thief), పోలీసులు (police), పోయింది (it's lost), ఎంబసీ (embassy). Memorise these cold — emergencies never wait for phrasebooks, and ten minutes of drilling buys total peace of mind.
topics.title: Emergency Telugu

topics.desc: మీరు or నువ్వు? రండి or రా? Respect levels, decoded with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: మీరు for every adult you don't know well — shopkeepers, officials, elders, strangers. నువ్వు waits for close friends, children and family. Wrong-side errors embarrass; learners are forgiven, but respect first is always safest.
faqs.q: When do I use మీరు?

faqs.a: Add -అండి: రా becomes రండి, వెళ్ళు becomes వెళ్లండి, చెప్పు becomes చెప్పండి. One ending, instant politeness — the highest-value suffix in Telugu.
faqs.q: How do I make a command polite?

faqs.a: అయ్యా (sir) and అమ్మగారు (madam) — or add గారు (gaaru) to any name: రాముగారు, లక్ష్మిగారు. Better than pointing and shouting in any language.
faqs.q: How do I address strangers?

topics.lede: మీరు or నువ్వు? రండి or రా? Respect levels, decoded.
topics.note: A note on గారు. గారు (gaaru) is Telugu's respect rocket — attach it to any name and watch warmth ignite: అమ్మగారు (respected mother/madam), అయ్యగారు (respected sir), రాముగారు. Two syllables that upgrade every introduction instantly.
paras: Telugu has two yous: మీరు (formal/plural — strangers, elders, officials) and నువ్వు (familiar — friends, children, family). English erased this distinction centuries ago; Telugu keeps it razor-sharp. Every conversation opens with an invisible choice — make it consciously, and make it respectful.

Verbs mirror the split: రండి (please come) versus రా (come!), చెప్పండి (please say) versus చెప్పు (say!), వెళ్లండి (please go) versus వెళ్ళు (go!). The -అండి ending is pure respect — same verb, different universe. Stem-alone orders bark; -అండి invites.

Giving and forgiving show the range: ఇవ్వండి (please give) versus ఇవ్వు (give!), క్షమించండి (please forgive) versus క్షమించు (forgive, familiar). Beggars and kings both hear ఇవ్వండి — politeness in Telugu costs nothing and buys everything.

Strangers get titles: అయ్యా (sir), అమ్మగారు (madam), అన్నయ్య (brother), అక్కయ్య (sister). అయ్యా, సహాయం చేయండి (sir, please help) opens any door; barking orders at strangers closes them. Telugu warmth is earned with two syllables of respect.
topics.title: Formal and informal Telugu

topics.desc: Verb-first sentences, నేను కావాలి, లేదు vs కాదు — fix the classic errors. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: English order with Telugu words: నేను వెళ్ళు instead of నేను వెళ్తున్నాను, verb first, question words misplaced. Cure: every sentence ends with the verb — practise SOV until English order feels foreign.
faqs.q: What is the most common mistake?

faqs.a: Wanting flows toward people: నాకు కావాలి (to-me it-is-wanted), never నేను కావాలి. One of Telugu's deepest patterns — experiences come TO you — and beginners fight it for weeks.
faqs.q: Why is నేను కావాలి wrong?

faqs.a: లేదు denies existence and possession — డబ్బు లేదు (no money); కాదు denies identity — నేను విద్యార్థిని కాదు (I am not a student). Two no's, two jobs, zero overlap.
faqs.q: లేదు or కాదు?

topics.lede: Verb-first sentences, నేను కావాలి, లేదు vs కాదు — fix them all.
topics.note: A note on తప్పు. తప్పు (tappu — mistake) is the kindest word in this lesson — నా తప్పు (my mistake) disarms every situation. Telugu people adore learners who err boldly and laugh warmly; the only true తప్పు is silence.
paras: Mistake one: English word order. నేను వెళ్ళు (I go — bare stem, wrong) instead of నేను వెళ్తున్నాను (I go — conjugated, right); verbs wandering mid-sentence instead of anchoring the end. Telugu is verb-final, always — SOV is not a suggestion, it is the law.

Mistake two: నేను కావాలి (I want — wrong) instead of నాకు కావాలి (to-me wanted — right). Telugu wanting flows toward the wanter; English wanting fires from the wanter. Flip the arrow and dozens of sentences — నాకు అర్థమైంది, నాకు తెలుసు — unlock at once.

Mistake three: one-size no. లేదు denies existence — డబ్బు లేదు (there's no money); కాదు denies identity — నేను ఉపాధ్యాయుడిని కాదు (I am not a teacher). Beginners spray లేదు everywhere; natives smile and correct. Learn both no's, use each precisely.

Mistake four: rushing sounds — flat long vowels, merged r's, skipped -అండి. నెమ్మదిగా (slowly), సరిగ్గా (correctly), మళ్లీ (again): the holy trinity of repair. ప్రయత్నం (effort) plus అభ్యాసం (practice) plus ఓపిక (patience) — and అభినందనలు, mistakes become fluency.
topics.title: Mistakes every learner makes

topics.desc: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud and brave first speeches. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Shadow natives: play a Telugu sentence, repeat it aloud half a second behind, matching rhythm and melody. Ten minutes daily rewires your mouth faster than any textbook.
faqs.q: What is the fastest speaking drill?

faqs.a: Yes — narrate your day in Telugu: నేను కాఫీ తాగుతున్నాను (I'm drinking coffee), నేను బడికి వెళ్తున్నాను. Thinking aloud turns dead time into speaking practice.
faqs.q: Should I talk to myself in Telugu?

faqs.a: Perfectionism. Telugu people reward every attempt and correct with love — మాట్లాడండి, తప్పు పర్లేదు (speak, mistakes are fine). Fluency is corrected mistakes, stacked daily.
faqs.q: What blocks speaking most?

links.label: Telugu practice lab

topics.note: A note on మాట్లాడదాం. మాట్లాడదాం (maatlaadaam — let's speak / we may speak) is permission and invitation in one word — రండి, తెలుగులో మాట్లాడదాం (come, let's speak in Telugu). Say it to every patient listener; doors, hearts and vocabularies open together.
paras: Speaking starts with shadowing: play a Telugu line, echo it half a beat behind, copying music more than words. సంభాషణ (conversation) is rhythm before grammar — shadow ten minutes daily and your mouth learns Telugu's dance while your brain watches.

Questions and answers volley practice: ప్రశ్న (question) out, సమాధానం (answer) back. Ask yourself everything — ఇది ఏమిటి? ఎక్కడ? ఎందుకు? — and answer aloud. Self-volleys feel silly for a day, then feel like fluency arriving.

Opinions and stories stretch speeches: అభిప్రాయం (opinion), నిజం (truth), కథ (story). నా అభిప్రాయం... (in my opinion...) forces full sentences; కథ చెప్పండి (tell a story) forces sequences. Opinions build sentences; stories build speakers.

Courage closes the circuit: ధైర్యం (courage) speaks first and perfects later. పాట (songs) loosen tongues, నవ్వు (laughter) dissolves fear, నిశ్శబ్దం (pauses) are allowed. Speak badly today — ప్రసంగం (speech) improves only in motion.
topics.title: Speaking practice

topics.desc: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Telugu sounds slow. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Spoken Telugu contracts: వెళ్తున్నాను melts toward వెళ్తున్నా, చేస్తున్నాను toward చేస్తున్నా. Learn the full forms first, then meet the street forms — this page bridges both.
faqs.q: Why is spoken Telugu so fast?

faqs.a: Children's films and songs first — clear speech, simple stories, endless repetition. Then రేడియో dramas, then full సినిమా (cinema). Difficulty ladders beat difficulty cliffs.
faqs.q: What should I listen to first?

faqs.a: Catch the question words — ఏమిటి, ఎక్కడ, ఎవరు, ఎప్పుడు — and the verb at the end. Questions plus verbs carry eighty percent of meaning; the rest is decoration.
faqs.q: How do I catch meaning in fast speech?

topics.note: A note on అర్థమైందా? అర్థమైందా? (arthamaindaa — do you understand?) is the kindest question in Telugu — teachers, friends and auto drivers ask it constantly. Answer అర్థమైంది (understood) or కొంచెం కొంచెం (little by little); honesty tunes every speaker to your level.
paras: Listening begins with attention: శ్రద్ధ (attention) — శ్రద్ధగా వినండి (listen carefully). Telugu sentences save the verb for last, so ears must hold the whole sentence before meaning lands. Patience is a listening skill; practise holding, not guessing.

Street Telugu contracts beautifully: వెళ్తున్నాను → వెళ్తున్నా, చదువుతున్నాను → చదువుతున్నా. Textbooks teach the full forms; ears must learn the melted ones. Listen for the verb-ghost at sentence end — the meaning hides there.

Media ladders the difficulty: పాట (songs) first — slow, repetitive, emotional; వార్తలు (news) next — clear, formal, standard; రేడియో (radio) drama third — fast, natural, fun; సినిమా (films) last — slang, speed, glory. Climb rung by rung; never leap.

Active listening closes the loop: మళ్లీ వినండి (listen again), ధ్వని (sound) by ధ్వని. Replay each line three times — once for music, once for words, once for meaning. Three passes per line, ten lines per day: ears transform within a month.
topics.title: Understanding spoken Telugu

topics.desc: Words to sentences to stories — reading Telugu from first signs to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Signboards: దుకాణం (shop), స్టేషన్ (station), హోటల్ (restaurant) — big letters, daily repetition, instant rewards. Streets teach faster than textbooks.
faqs.q: What should I read first?

faqs.a: Children's books — short వాక్యం (sentences), pictures for context, full gunintalu. Then comics, then వార్తాపత్రిక headlines, then articles.
faqs.q: When am I ready for books?

faqs.a: Keep a నిఘంటువు (dictionary) app open and mine unknown words — five per page, no more. Reading with a dictionary beats studying word lists: context glues memory.
faqs.q: How do I handle unknown words?

topics.lede: Words to sentences to stories — reading from first signs to full pages.
topics.note: A note on వార్తాపత్రిక. Telugu newspapers — ఈనాడు, సాక్షి — use formal written Telugu, nobler than street speech. Headlines first: big type, short lines, daily habit. One headline a day keeps illiteracy away.
paras: Reading starts with words: పదం (word) by పదం — చదవండి (please read) signs, labels, names. Telugu spelling mirrors speech, so sounding out works: see దుకాణం, say dukaanam, know shop. Phonetic scripts reward beginners richly.

Sentences assemble next: వాక్యం (sentence) — subject, object, verb-last. Read SOV sentences end-first for meaning: find the verb, then ask who-did-what. Backwards parsing feels odd for a week, then automatic forever.

Paragraphs and articles follow: పేరా (paragraph), వ్యాసం (article), కవిత (poem). Children's stories first — short, illustrated, kind — then పత్రిక (magazines), then సాహిత్యం (literature) itself. Telugu's written heritage spans a thousand years; start at the shallow end.

Dictionaries deepen everything: నిఘంటువు (dictionary) — five new words per page, written down, reviewed nightly. Reading without recording entertains; reading with recording teaches. Mine every page; keep every gem.
topics.title: Reading Telugu

topics.desc: Letters to lists to letters — writing Telugu from first strokes to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Round strokes before all: Telugu letters flow circular — అ, ఆ, ఉ, ఎ — so practise circles and hooks first. Trace big, shrink slowly; చేతిరాత (handwriting) beautifies with mileage.
faqs.q: How do I start writing Telugu?

faqs.a: జాబితా (lists): shopping lists, word lists, daily plans. Lists forgive grammar, demand spelling, and get used — the perfect beginner writing.
faqs.q: What should I write first?

faqs.a: ఉత్తరం (letters) to friends, గమనిక (notes) to self, ఇంటిపని (homework) for courses. Real writing to real readers beats copied exercises every time.
faqs.q: When real writing?

topics.lede: Letters to lists to letters — writing from first strokes to full pages.
topics.note: A note on సంతకం. Your సంతకం (signature) in Telugu script is a milestone — practise it until it flows in one confident motion. Signing Telugu-style on forms, cards and letters declares belonging more than any certificate.
paras: Writing starts with strokes: Telugu letters curve and loop — రాయండి (please write) circles, hooks and waves before full letters. Trace అ ఆ ఇ ఈ ఉ ఊ big and slow; the hand learns shapes the eye already knows.
Tools matter little, mileage matters all: కలం (pen), pencil, finger on steamed mirrors — Telugu children trace in rice, sand and air. Write everywhere; medium is vanity, motion is learning.

Lists graduate the hand: జాబితా (list) — గమనిక (notes), చిరునామా (addresses), తేదీ (dates). Copy your own పేరు (name) fifty times, then friends' names, then street names. Familiar words, fresh script: the fastest fluent hand.

Real writing arrives: ఉత్తరం (letters), దరఖాస్తు (applications), పరీక్ష (exams), ఇంటిపని (homework). Write a postcard to yourself in Telugu — short, joyful, posted. First posted Telugu is never forgotten.
topics.title: Writing Telugu

topics.desc: Who does what, verb last — Telugu sentences decoded with living examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Subject-Object-Verb: నేను పుస్తకం చదువుతున్నాను (I book read). Endings mark roles, so order flexes for emphasis — but verb-last is home.
faqs.q: What is Telugu word order?

faqs.a: Tense lives on the verb: వెళ్తున్నాను (go-present), వెళ్లాను (went), వెళ్తాను (will go). Time words — నిన్న, ఈరోజు, రేపు — frame it; the verb carries it.
faqs.q: How do tenses work?

faqs.a: Add -ఆ and rise: అది నీ పుస్తకమా? (is that your book?). Question words — ఏమిటి, ఎక్కడ, ఎవరు — sit where the answer would.
faqs.q: How do I ask questions?

topics.lede: Who does what, verb last — sentences decoded with living examples.
topics.note: A note on వాన పడుతోంది. Telugu weather does things: వాన పడుతోంది (rain falls), ఎండ కొడుతోంది (sun strikes), గాలి వీస్తోంది (wind blows). No empty it — Telugu skies act. Weather sentences teach SOV with zero confusion: subject, then verb, done.
paras: Simple sentences stack three blocks: నేను బడికి వెళ్తున్నాను (I — to-school — go), ఆమె పాట పాడుతోంది (she — song — sings), మేము తెలుగు చదువుతున్నాం (we — Telugu — study). Subject, object, verb — build a hundred of these and Telugu skeleton is yours.

Animals make perfect practice: పిల్లవాడు నవ్వుతున్నాడు (the boy laughs), కుక్క మొరుగుతోంది (the dog barks), పిల్లి నిద్రపోతోంది (the cat sleeps). Short subjects, vivid verbs, zero ambiguity — describe every creature you meet and SOV becomes reflex.

Time flexes the frame: నేను రేపు వస్తాను (I'll come tomorrow), నిన్న వాన పడింది (it rained yesterday). Time words float — front for emphasis, middle for flow — while the verb holds the end. Tense plus time word: past, present, future, mastered.

Identity and questions close the set: ఇది నా ఇల్లు (this is my house), అది నీ పుస్తకమా? (is that your book?), అంతా బాగుంది (all is well). Equate with ఇది/అది, question with -ఆ, reassure with అంతా బాగుంది — sentences for every situation.
topics.title: Telugu sentence structure

topics.desc: Rahul becomes రాహుల్ — spell, write and own your name in Telugu script. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sound it out in Telugu letters: Rahul → రాహుల్, Priya → ప్రియా, John → జాన్. Telugu spells by ear — say your name slowly, catch each sound, write each letter.
faqs.q: How do I write my name in Telugu?

faqs.a: Loan letters — జ (ja), హ (ha), శ ష స (sha/sa) — handle foreign sounds. జాన్ (John), హోటల్ (hotel) — borrowed letters for borrowed names, fully Telugu now.
faqs.q: What about sounds Telugu lacks?

faqs.a: మొదటి అక్షరం (first letter) starts it, చివరి అక్షరం (last letter) ends it. Introduce with నా పేరు... (my name is...), then write it — introductions stick twice as well written.
faqs.q: How do I introduce my name?

topics.lede: Rahul becomes రాహుల్ — spell, write and own your name in Telugu.
topics.note: A note on రాహుల్ vs రాహుల్. The ha glides in Telugu names — Rahul appears as రాహుల్ or రాహుల్ with a soft హ, sometimes even రావుల్. All are read Rahul; none is wrong. Telugu welcomes foreign names with flexible spelling — pick the shape you love and own it.
paras: Names transliterate by ear: break yours into sounds, match each to Telugu letters — శ్రీను (Srinu), లక్ష్మి (Lakshmi), వెంకట్ (Venkat) show the pattern. Say it slow, write it true — స్పెల్లింగ్ (spelling) by sound, not by English letters.
Foreign sounds borrow loan letters: జ for John (జాన్), హ for hotels and Rahuls, శ for Sharma sounds. These Sanskrit-born letters are Telugu citizens now — use them proudly for every imported sound.

Introductions pair speech and script: పరిచయం (introduction) — నా పేరు... (my name is...), spoken, then written. పేరు బోర్డులు (name boards) on doors and desks teach daily — read every board, collect every name.

Nicknames warm everything: ముద్దుపేరు (nickname) — బంగారం (gold/darling), కన్నా (dear), చిన్నోడు (little one). Telugu shortens with love: Srinivas becomes శ్రీను, Lakshmi becomes లచ్చి. Earn a Telugu nickname and you have arrived.
topics.title: Write your name in Telugu

topics.desc: అదిరింది, మామా, వేరే లెవెల్ — street Telugu that films, friends and fun run on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: సూపర్ (super) and అదిరింది (rocked) — positive, universal, safe. Sprinkle them on food, films and friends; instant insider status.
faqs.q: What slang is safe everywhere?

faqs.a: మామా (dude) — for friends only, never elders or strangers. Friendship slang misused offends; rightly used, it bonds instantly.
faqs.q: Can I call people maamaa?

faqs.a: ఊరికే (just like that / for fun) — ఊరికే చెప్పాను (just kidding), ఊరికే వచ్చాను (just dropped by). The most Telugu word in existence: purposeless joy, declared proudly.
faqs.q: What does oorike mean?

topics.lede: అదిరింది, మామా, వేరే లెవెల్ — street Telugu that fun runs on.
topics.note: A note on ఊరికే. ఊరికే (oorike) defies translation — just because, for fun, no reason, chill. ఎందుకు? — ఊరికే (why? — just because). Whole philosophies hide in three syllables; use it freely, smile always.
paras: Praise slang opens doors: సూపర్ (super), అదిరింది (rocked it), వేరే లెవెల్ (next level), దంచేశావ్ (you smashed it), అబ్బా (wow). Food, films, friends' outfits — praise everything loudly. Telugu people praise generously; learners should too.

Friendship words bond crews: మామా (dude), రా (hey come), అరేయ్ (hey!) — friends-only, always warm. అరేయ్ మామా (hey dude) starts a thousand conversations daily. Never aim them upward at elders; sideways at friends, fire freely.

Reaction words colour stories: అయ్యో (oh no!), అబ్బా (wow!), కథలు చెప్పకు (stop making things up!). Telugu storytelling runs on reactions — gasp, laugh, disbelieve theatrically. Flat faces kill stories; big reactions feed them.

Playful edges season everything: పోరా (get lost — playful among friends, rude otherwise), ఛీ (disgust, mild), ఊరికే (just because). Learn the edges, respect the edges: slang's power is knowing exactly where fun ends.
topics.title: Telugu slang

topics.desc: Toys, moons, stars and good-child gold — Telugu for little learners, big joy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Songs and కథ (stories) — పాట with actions, tales with voices. Children absorb Telugu through music and play long before grammar.
faqs.q: How do kids learn Telugu best?

faqs.a: మంచి పిల్లవాడు / మంచి పిల్ల (good boy / good girl) — praise every attempt loudly. Telugu parenting runs on encouragement; learners of all ages bloom under it.
faqs.q: How do I praise a child?

faqs.a: ఆట (games): name objects — బంతి! బొమ్మ! — count steps, sing counts. Play first, words hitchhike.
faqs.q: Games or lessons?

topics.lede: Toys, moons, stars and gold stars — Telugu for little learners, big joy.
topics.note: A note on బంగారం. బంగారం (bangaaram — gold/darling) melts every Telugu heart — నా బంగారం (my darling) for children, pets and beloveds. Terms of endearment are Telugu's mother tongue; every child swims in them.
paras: Little learners start with love: పిల్లలు (children), పాప (baby), బంగారం (darling), మంచి పిల్లవాడు (good boy). Telugu childhood floats on affection-words — call every child బంగారం and watch faces light like దీపావళి.
Play teaches fastest: ఆట (play), బొమ్మ (toy), బంతి (ball) — ఆడుకుందాం (let's play)! Count throws, name colours, chase and giggle. Play first; Telugu hitchhikes on joy.
School words structure days: బడి (school), ఉపాధ్యాయుడు (teacher), పాఠం (lesson), ఇంటిపని (homework). నమస్కారం టీచర్ (hello teacher) opens every school day — respect and learning, hand in hand.

Sky words spark wonder: సూర్యుడు (sun), చందమామ (moon), నక్షత్రం (star) — చందమామ చూడు (look at the moon)! Night-sky Telugu, whispered on terraces, becomes lifelong memory. Teach the sky; the child keeps the language.
